Mahomes now has multiple scoring strikes and zero interceptions in three straight games, and Sunday's five TD tosses represented a new season high. items.headline: Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards.
items.summary: Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. items.headline: Prescott completed 30 of 51 passes for 343 yards with five touchdowns and one interception while rushing four times for seven yards in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday. He also ran for a two-point conversion.
items.summary: Playing catch-up from the second quarter on did wonders for Prescott's fantasy production, as the veteran quarterback sent 38 total targets in the direction of the talented trio of George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy alone. Prescott connected with Pickens for three of his scoring strikes, which went for 35, 39 and five yards. Flournoy (11 yards) and Lamb (one yard) accounted for the final two in the fourth quarter, and Prescott added a two-point conversion run after the final scoring toss with an admirable diving attempt on which he made contact with the pylon with the extended ball. Prescott tied a career high with his TD pass total, while his passing yardage was a season high. He should have an opportunity to put together a successful encore next Sunday, as a Week 11 home matchup with the vulnerable Titans secondary awaits.

items.headline: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added two carries for 21 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
items.summary: As expected, Sunday's showdown between the longtime rivals turned into a complete offensive showcase, and Purdy was right at the center of the fireworks. The veteran quarterback recorded a career-high passing yardage total, with his 66-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey with just over three minutes remaining putting Purdy over the top. That TD toss was preceded by 11- and 74-yard scoring strikes to Deebo Samuel and McCaffrey, respectively, in the first half, giving Purdy his third tally of at least three touchdown passes this season. Purdy's 78.6 percent completion rate also was his second-highest total of the season, and the fact the star signal-caller seemed to have quick chemistry with trade-deadline acquisition Keenan Allen bodes very well, considering Purdy also may have Mike Evans (Achilles) back for next Sunday night's Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings.

items.headline: Flowers brought in six of seven targets for 74 yards and lost a fumble in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
items.summary: After being held to just three catches for six yards over the previous two games while Joe Fagnano primarily led the Ravens offense, Flowers got a major reprieve in the form of the debuting Jacoby Brissett. The talented wideout took advantage by finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for Baltimore on the night, but Flowers had the ball stripped from him after a 15-yard catch at the Chargers' 46-yard line with 2:11 remaining. The lost fumble turned out to effectively snuff out the Ravens' chances of realistically getting into position for a potential game-tying field goal, ending the game on a sour note. Nevertheless, the fact Brissett threw for 340 yards in his first game in the offense bodes well for Flowers' prospects as a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers on Sunday approaches.

items.headline: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
items.summary: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.headline: Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Monangai (toe) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's practice estimate.
items.summary: Monangai told Courtney Cronin of ESPN on Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints, and after being spotted in full pads at Tuesday's unofficial practice, the running back would have logged an uncapped session one day later if the team had held drills. Monangai is seeking his first game action since Week 4, when he initially suffered a turf toe injury and a right thumb concern.

items.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai says he's 'on track' to return Sunday against Saints
items.summary: Bears running back Kyle Monangai said Monday that he's "on track" to return Sunday against the Saints after sitting out five games because of a thumb injury and turf toe.

items.headline: Chase brought in 11 of 14 targets for 231 yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Cincinnati.
items.summary: Chase posted one of his signature 200-yard performances, with Sunday night's qualifying as the fourth of his storied career and marking his third instance accomplishing it against an AFC North rival. Needless to say, all three components of Chase's receiving line led the Bengals by a wide margin on the night as well, and after failing to hit the century mark in yardage in any of the first six games of the season, the star wideout has recorded at least 141 receiving yards in three straight. Chase is now up to a 64-878-7 line on 87 targets across nine games heading into a Week 11 Monday night home road matchup against the Commanders on Nov. 23.

items.headline: Bengals' Burrow, Chase, Higgins add Spanish flair to TD celebrations in Madrid
items.summary: The Bengals' first-half lead called for celebrations inspired by being in Spain.

items.headline: Higgins (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: It's a new "injury" for Higgins, but the full participation level suggests it's nothing serious after the wideout was managed late in last Sunday night's blowout win over the Steelers, per Kelsey Conway of The Cincinnati Enquirer. Higgins already has a fantasy-friendly 53 catches (on 73 targets) for 824 yards and six touchdowns through nine games. He's on pace for a career year in 2026.

items.headline: Bengals' Burrow, Chase, Higgins add Spanish flair to TD celebrations in Madrid
items.summary: The Bengals' first-half lead called for celebrations inspired by being in Spain.

items.headline: Ferguson didn't practice Wednesday due to knee and ankle injuries and won't be available for Sunday's game against the Titans, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Ferguson injured his knee in a Week 9 win over the Colts, while the ankle issue is more of a lingering concern after he initially sustained a low sprain in a Week 8 loss to the Cardinals. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer previously announced Nov. 9 that Ferguson was set to miss multiple weeks, so the tight end's continued absence from practice comes as little surprise. In Ferguson's stead, Brevyn Spann-Ford should be in line for another turn as Dallas' top tight end in Week 11.

items.headline: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.headline: Lamb secured seven of 13 targets for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: Despite his own impressive numbers, Lamb played second fiddle to George Pickens for a change, as the latter doubled up the former in receptions and did the same with a yard to spare in receiving yards. Nevertheless, Lamb still put together a solid performance that included his eighth touchdown reception of the season, a spectacular leaping one-handed one-yard grab late in the fourth quarter. Lamb now is up to five consecutive double-digit target tallies and has at least 70 receiving yards in four of the last five contests heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the vulnerable Titans defense.

items.headline: Week 9 winners and losers: Lamb, Walker come up big, Gibbs, Taylor disappoint
items.summary: CeeDee Lamb and Kenneth Walker III came up big in Week 9, while Jahmyr Gibbs and Jonathan Taylor were quieter than usual.

items.headline: Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

items.headline: Cowboys WR Pickens, CB Porter, LB Overshown inactive against Colts
items.summary: The Cowboys will be without wide receiver George Pickens, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown against the Colts.

items.headline: The Cowboys placed Goodson (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.

items.headline: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.summary: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.headline: Miller agreed Tuesday to sign with Dallas as a member of the practice squad, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.summary: Miller will move on to the second organization of his career, after the Saints waived the fourth-year running back last week. Before getting cut loose, the 24-year-old carried 57 times for 159 yards (2.8 average) and two touchdowns to go with nine receptions for 37 yards on 13 targets over six games. Despite his lack of efficiency with New Orleans, Miller may not have to wait long to get a look as the Cowboys' No. 2 running back. He'll join Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin on the practice squad, and one or two of the trio will likely be elevated for Sunday's game against the 49ers since Javonte Williams is currently the only healthy back on Dallas' 53-man roster.

items.headline: Saints activate WR Jordyn Tyson, LT Kelvin Banks, cut RB Kendre Miller
items.summary: Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. have been activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.

items.headline: Fantasy football matchup ranks: Upgrade Jonah Coleman, downgrade Brock Purdy
items.summary: The most and least favorable matchups in the NFL for this week's games at the four key fantasy positions.

items.headline: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
items.summary: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Yates and Clay debate Ryan Flournoy vs. Courtland Sutton in Week 11
items.summary: Yates and Clay debate Ryan Flournoy vs. Courtland Sutton in Week 11

items.headline: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
items.summary: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

items.headline: Should Jared Goff be in fantasy lineups each and every week?
items.summary: Should Jared Goff be in fantasy lineups each and every week?

items.headline: Goff completed 20 of 31 passes for 303 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munich. He added three yards on his only carry.
items.summary: A potential barn burner versus Drake Maye never materialized when the New England quarterback left the game early with an ankle injury, but Goff and the Detroit offense still held up their end of the bargain. Two of Goff's TDs went to Amon-Ra St. Brown, including a 56-yard catch-and-run score in the first quarter, while Isaac TeSlaa also hauled in a 12-yard score in the second. Goff will take an 18:4 TD:INT through nine games into a Week 11 clash at home against the Buccaneers.

items.headline: Is Sam LaPorta a starting fantasy TE right now?
items.summary: Is Sam LaPorta a starting fantasy TE right now?

items.headline: LaPorta caught one of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Patriots in Munch.
items.summary: The Lions didn't need to throw it much, as Drake Maye (ankle) got knocked out of the game for the Patriots early, and LaPorta simply didn't get many chances to make an impact. It was the worst performance of the season for the fourth-year tight end, but LaPorta's gone four straight games without reaching 40 receiving yards or getting into the end zone. He'll try to break out in Week 11 against the Buccaneers.

items.headline: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

items.headline: Does Packers' Christian Watson + Matthew Golden = 3,000 yards?
items.summary: Watson and Golden are on pace to join a rare club of WR pairs who combined for 3,000 yards.

items.headline: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
items.summary: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

items.headline: Does Packers' Christian Watson + Matthew Golden = 3,000 yards?
items.summary: Watson and Golden are on pace to join a rare club of WR pairs who combined for 3,000 yards.

items.headline: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

items.headline: Kayshon Boutte rises to make an awesome grab for a Texans TD
items.summary: Kayshon Boutte rises to make an awesome grab for a Texans TD

items.headline: Collins secured three of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
items.summary: Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: C.J. Stroud fires a 42-yard dime to Nico Collins for Texans TD
items.summary: C.J. Stroud fires a 42-yard dime to Nico Collins for Texans TD

items.headline: Klein secured all four targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
items.summary: Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: C.J. Stroud finds Marlin Klein for his 3rd passing TD
items.summary: C.J. Stroud finds Marlin Klein for his 3rd passing TD

items.headline: Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards and brought in three of four targets for 17 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
items.summary: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

items.headline: DE Danielle Hunter, LB Azeez Al-Shaair among Texans ruled out vs. Browns
items.summary: The Texans will be without a number of key starters -- including running back David Montgomery and All-Pro defensive end Danielle Hunter -- when they travel to face the Browns.

items.headline: Dell secured three of four targets for 27 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
items.summary: The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: 'Grateful' Tank Dell has 105 receiving yards in 2nd game back from knee injury
items.summary: Texans WR Tank Dell scored a touchdown Sunday in his second game back from a gruesome knee injury.

items.headline: Mike Clay: Tyler Warren is not startable in fantasy
items.summary: Mike Clay: Tyler Warren is not startable in fantasy

items.headline: Warren brought in one of five targets for 22 yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
items.summary: The talented tight end's production continued to suffer collateral damage from Daniel Jones' poor play, but Warren did provide a useful gain on his one catch. The 2025 first-round pick now has recorded Thursday's yardage total or less in three of the last four games, but Warren's outlook may change if Jones, who James Boyd of The Athletic reports head coach Shane Steichen wouldn't rule out demoting when asked after the game, is replaced by Anthony Richardson or Riley Leonard under center.

items.headline: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.
items.summary: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Travis Hunter makes Jessie Bates' Jaguars trade a hit with his nephews
items.summary: The safety's young nephews were thrilled to learn their uncle would be Hunter's teammate.

items.headline: Lawrence completed 25 of 35 passes for 352 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans. He added 27 yards on four carries.
items.summary: It was another huge performance from the 27-year-old QB, as Lawrence set a new season high in passing yards and threw at least three TDs for the fifth time in nine games to begin the year. He spread the ball around again, as seven different Jaguars caught multiple passes and Parker Washington, Josh Cameron and Brenton Strange were all on the other end of scores. Lawrence will take a sharp 21:5 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Giants.

items.headline: Adam Rank: Trevor Lawrence needs to be a must-start fantasy QB every week
items.summary: Adam Rank: Trevor Lawrence needs to be a must-start fantasy QB every week

items.headline: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
items.summary: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

items.headline: Jaguars rebuff trade interest in WR Brian Thomas Jr.
items.summary: Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. wasn't traded Tuesday by the NFL's trade deadline.

items.headline: Tuten (ankle/foot), per head coach Liam Coen, "will maybe run around a little bit" at Friday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
items.summary: Tuten did not get any work in Thursday after being limited at Wednesday's practice, but Coen's comments suggest he could be back on the field Friday. Tuten was listed as either limited or as a non-participant the last eight times the Jaguars released an injury report but has not missed a game, so while his status is up in the air there is reason to believe he will be out there Sunday. Tuten's status for Week 11 will officially be revealed when the Jaguars release their next injury report later Friday.

items.headline: How Bhayshul Tuten became the clear No. 1 running back for the Jaguars
items.summary: After a lackluster rookie season, Tuten ranks 14th in NFL in rushing yards entering Sunday's game against the Giants.

items.headline: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
items.summary: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

items.headline: Eric Moody: Parker Washington firmly on the WR1 radar in Week 11
items.summary: Eric Moody: Parker Washington firmly on the WR1 radar in Week 11

items.headline: Kelce was a full participant in Wednesday's practice despite being listed with ankle and calf injuries.
items.summary: During this past Sunday's 35-13 win over the Falcons, Kelce exited for a brief spell in the first half after injuring his ankle, but he ultimately returned to the contest. In addition to the ankle issue, Kelce may have tweaked his calf at some point in Week 10, but head coach Andy Reid indicated prior to Wednesday's practice that the veteran tight end is "doing well" in his recovery from the injuries, per Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com. His ability to take every rep for the Chiefs' first Week 11 session suggests his status for Sunday's game againt the Cardinals isn't in any peril.

items.headline: Week 11 offers another impressive milestone for Travis Kelce
items.summary: Nate Taylor discusses Travis Kelce ahead of his 100th game at Arrowhead Stadium.

items.headline: According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN,  Adams (hamstring) is believed to be targeting a return to action Nov. 25 against the Packers.
items.summary: Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.

items.headline: Sean McVay: Rams optimistic WR Davante Adams will return 'sooner than later'
items.summary: The Rams are optimistic that injured wide receiver Davante Adams will return from his hamstring injury "sooner than later," coach Sean McVay said.

items.headline: The Rams signed Presley to their practice squad Tuesday, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Presley has been a regular on the Rams' practice squad since signing with the club as an undrafted free agent in April of 2025. He joined the 53-man roster for the first time Nov. 12 and was cut four days later, but he's going to stay with the organization on the practice squad. Presley hasn't logged a touch or a target in either of his two NFL regular-season games to date, so he should be considered depth for a wideout corps that has been without both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring).

items.headline: Rams put WR Puka Nacua on IR with knee, toe injuries
items.summary: The Rams, who had said they would not put Puka Nacua on IR, pivoted so they can sign Brennan Presley to the active roster and Tyler Scott to the practice squad.

items.headline: Miami Dolphins backup QB Kyle McCord showed poise in debut vs. Indianapolis Colts
items.summary: Miami coach Jeff Hafley praised McCord's poise and the trust he showed in receivers Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas.

items.headline: McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed twice for four yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble that was returned for a touchdown.
items.summary: Drawing his first career start as a result of Malik Willis having gone on injured reserve with an abdomen injury earlier in the week, McCord acquitted himself well overall in a favorable matchup. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles spread the ball around to nine different targets, and he had a statement three-yard touchdown run on the first play of the fourth quarter when he powered through a pair of defenders and broke the plane despite having his facemask pulled. McCord's one turnover was very costly, however, as it was recovered on the Dolphins' six-yard line and returned for a short touchdown. McCord should only get more comfortable by following up Sunday's solid showing with another week of practice, but he'll draw a tough Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

items.headline: Miami Dolphins backup QB Kyle McCord showed poise in debut vs. Indianapolis Colts
items.summary: Miami coach Jeff Hafley praised McCord's poise and the trust he showed in receivers Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas.

items.headline: Washington secured all three targets for 50 yards, threw a 34-yard touchdown on his one pass attempt and returned four punts for 36 yards in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Washington finished second in receiving yards for the Dolphins and also was partly responsible for the team's one score through the air, uncorking a well-thrown 34-yard strike to Jalen Tolbert on a trick play. Washington also continued to produce in his returner role, and he's now up to 812 all-purpose yards through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Bills next Sunday.

items.headline: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
items.summary: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

items.headline: Vikings WR Jauan Jennings on rebuffing return to 49ers: 'I love where I'm at'
items.summary: Jauan Jennings said he rebuffed the chance to return to the 49ers via trade despite struggling to produce for the Vikings because "I love where I'm at."

items.headline: Jones carried the ball 11 times for 47 yards and a touchdown and caught his only target for eight yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
items.summary: Jordan Mason led the Vikings with 59 rushing yards, but Jones had the more productive afternoon as he scored his first TD since Week 5 on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Jones' upside will remain limited while working in a timeshare with Mason, but he's still got some utility heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

items.summary: How Aaron Jones Sr. helped this military veteran

items.headline: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
items.summary: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

items.headline: Vikings left at QB crossroads after Carson Wentz's poor MNF showing vs. Bills
items.summary: After a historically poor performance by Carson Wentz on Monday night, Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell was asked whether the team might trade for a QB ahead of Tuesday's deadline. He deferred the question to GM Nolan Teasley.

items.headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that Addison underwent thumb surgery earlier this week and won't be placed on injured reserve, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Thus, the Vikings are expecting Addison to recover fully before the four games required of an IR stint, but in any case he will miss some time due to the thumb injury he suffered in practice last Friday and sidelined him this past Sunday at Green Bay. With Addison out of the lineup, Minnesota will be relying on Justin Jefferson, Jauan Jennings (calf), Myles Price, Tai Felton and Jeshaun Jones at wide receiver.

items.headline: Vikings WR Jordan Addison needs thumb surgery, is candidate for IR
items.summary: Vikings wide receiver Jordan Addison needs to undergo surgery on his thumb and is a candidate for injured reserve, coach Kevin O'Connell said Monday.

items.headline: Drake Maye ankle injury: Is the Patriots' season over? Can Tommy DeVito step up?
items.summary: If the QB doesn't return in 2026, New England faces an uphill battle against some of the NFL's best teams.

items.headline: Mike Reiss of ESPN.com notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action.
items.summary: Regarding Maye's status going forward, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'll wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but he also acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Sunday, Nov. 29 against the Chargers and possibly beyond. That said, as NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests, New England is expected to explore the QB market in the coming days, be it through a practice squad addition or a veteran free agent such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who previously worked with  offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

items.headline: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

items.headline: Source: Pats' Rhamondre Stevenson expected to miss time with knee tendon issue
items.summary: Patriots top running back Rhamondre Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that is not expected to require surgery but could sideline him for a short period of time, a source told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

items.headline: Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
items.summary: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

items.headline: Fantasy football free agent pickups: Mendoza, Douglas, Estime among top options
items.summary: Eric Karabell lists the top available players in most leagues, including the No. 1 pick in the draft.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Bye-mageddon means getting comfortable with the uncomfortable
items.summary: A bye-laden Week 11 might make you cringe at some of your lineup decisions, so let the facts hone your feelings on Bo Nix, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, Stefon Diggs and Colston Loveland.

items.headline: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

items.headline: Fantasy football: Don't be surprised if Likely is TE1, Gainwell finishes strong
items.summary: Eric Karabell explains why the Giants' TE could top the position and the Bucs' No. 2 RB will finish strong.

items.headline: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
items.summary: Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Jets QB Geno Smith suffers ankle injury, replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik
items.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter and was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.

items.headline: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
items.summary: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

items.headline: Garrett Wilson vs. Carnell Tate: Clay and Yates pick a side for Week 11
items.summary: Garrett Wilson vs. Carnell Tate: Clay and Yates pick a side for Week 11

items.headline: Wilson (concussion) caught seven of 14 targets for 106 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Wilson set a new season high in targets and came one yard short of his Week 3 season high Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. His production came on a mix of passes from Geno Smith (ankle) and rookie Cade Klubnik, the latter of whom saw his first NFL action after Smith exited in the second half. Wilson figures to work as the top target for whomever starts under center in a Week 11 road game against the Chargers.

items.headline: Field Yates voices his concerns for Saquon Barkley in fantasy
items.summary: Field Yates voices his concerns for Saquon Barkley in fantasy

items.headline: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

items.headline: NFL outlines steps in Jalen Hurts investigation in letter to senator
items.summary: The NFL provided some additional details about the investigation into how Jalen Hurts' blood clots were handled in response to an inquiry from a U.S. senator.

items.headline: The Philadelphia Eagles' 2026 trade haul is likely to age well over time
items.summary: Whether Philadelphia wants to go after its QB of the future or build up around Jalen Hurts, it has options.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Bye-mageddon means getting comfortable with the uncomfortable
items.summary: A bye-laden Week 11 might make you cringe at some of your lineup decisions, so let the facts hone your feelings on Bo Nix, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, Stefon Diggs and Colston Loveland.

items.headline: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
items.summary: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

items.headline: Black rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys. He added two catches for 13 yards on two targets.
items.summary: The rookie running back has tallied double-digit carries in three straight games and played 26 of 65 offensive snaps behind Christian McCaffrey's 39 snaps. CMC was also extremely productive out of the backfield against Dallas' Swiss-cheese defense, turning 17 touches into 243 total yards and three touchdowns. Black is more involved than most of McCaffrey's backups have been in recent seasons, and the rookie is offering some standalone RB2/3 valuation in one of the league's most efficient offenses. Over the last three games, Black has rushed 34 times for 186 yards (5.5 YPC) and two touchdowns.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Kaelon Black and Malik Willis lead the way
items.summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.headline: 49ers put up big numbers vs. Cowboys, tout 'incredibly dangerous' offense
items.summary: The 49ers racked up 584 yards against the Cowboys on Sunday in a jaw-dropping offensive display led by Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel.

items.headline: Samuel rushed three times for 78 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 31 yards and another score in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: Samuel made his return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury, and the versatile veteran was put right to work as the de facto No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) still sidelined. Samuel came just a yard short of tying his single-game career high in rushing yards, and his receiving and rushing touchdowns came from 11 and 70 yards out, respectively. Samuel has five total touchdowns through six games heading into a Week 11 home matchup against a tough Vikings defense next Sunday night.

items.headline: Watkins caught two passes for 49 yards on three targets in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys.
items.summary: With Deebo Samuel still working his way back to 100 percent off his hamstring injury, Keenan Allen being eased in after his acquisition from the Colts and Mike Evans (Achilles) remaining inactive, Watkins' 44 snaps led San Francisco's wideouts. However, his three targets were a distant fourth on the team and represented just a 10.7 percent share. Allen will likely play more moving forward, and Evans is expected back in the bear future. Watkins doesn't have much fantasy appeal as an ancillary option.

items.headline: The key behind 49ers' 7-1 start? Big contributions from the team's youth
items.summary: While the 49ers' stars have shown out, Jordan Watkins, Jaden Dugger and Kaelon Black have also led the team to its best start since 2019.

items.headline: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Seahawks are hurting with injuries, but two players will return vs. Raiders
items.summary: QB Drew Lock will start again for Darnold. And LB Uchenna Nwosu and WR Rashid Shaheed will return to the field in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 144-yard quarter sparks Seahawks in win over Raiders
items.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, finished with a season-high 171 yards on eight catches, with 144 coming in the third quarter to help the Seahawks turn a three-point halftime deficit into a 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.

items.headline: Smith-Njigba gathered in eight of 10 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 21-13 win at Las Vegas.
items.summary: Smith-Njigba's Week 10 performance was fueled by a 71-yard catch and run for a touchdown in the middle of the third quarter, but he still was able to put up 100 yards on his other seven receptions en route to a new season high in the category. As the Seahawks hit their Week 11 bye, he's reached the century mark in receiving eight times and resides on a 79-1,207-10 line on 109 targets through 10 contests. Smith-Njigba's next chance to continue aggravating opposing defenses arrives Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

items.headline: Why Field Yates recommends benching Emeka Egbuka in Week 11
items.summary: Why Field Yates recommends benching Emeka Egbuka in Week 11

items.headline: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Fantasy football: Don't be surprised if Likely is TE1, Gainwell finishes strong
items.summary: Eric Karabell explains why the Giants' TE could top the position and the Bucs' No. 2 RB will finish strong.

items.headline: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Irving, Walker III, Bowers and more Knockout league pickups for Week 11
items.summary: As the number of teams shrink, the number of stars available in Knockout leagues grows. Here are the ones to get.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

items.headline: Mayfield (foot/right thumb) officially was limited at Thursday's practice.
items.summary: Mayfield came out of the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye with a foot injury, which kept him out of drills Wednesday. After resuming on-field work Thursday, he relayed to Scott Smith of the team's official site that he felt good and was "limited," the latter of which has been confirmed. Per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano, Mayfield also said, "If I feel like [Jalon Daniels] gives us a better chance to win, I have no shame in admitting that." As a result, it appears as if both Mayfield and Daniels have a chance to be under center for Tampa Bay on Sunday at Detroit.

items.headline: Bucs QB Baker Mayfield hopes to play Sunday despite foot injury: 'I feel ready'
items.summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is hoping to play Sunday against the Lions after he sustained a foot injury two weeks ago against the Chicago Bears.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Flournoy, Ayomanor among top candidates
items.summary: There is no busier bye week than this one. Matt Bowen lists potential options if you need a fill-in.

items.headline: Ayomanor caught five of 10 targets for 79 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: While he wasn't particularly efficient with the volume, Ayomanor led the Titans in targets and receiving yards on the afternoon, , and the receptions and yardage were both career highs, with Carnell Tate (shoulder) sidelined and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) exiting the contest early. If they both remain on the shelf in Week 11 against the Cowboys, Ayomanor figures to handle an increased role once again. The second-year WR sports an 18-290-1 line on 36 targets through nine games on the year.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Bye-mageddon means getting comfortable with the uncomfortable
items.summary: A bye-laden Week 11 might make you cringe at some of your lineup decisions, so let the facts hone your feelings on Bo Nix, Tony Pollard, Jaylen Warren, Chris Olave, Malik Nabers, Stefon Diggs and Colston Loveland.

items.headline: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Commanders QB Sam Hartman to star as 'The Bachelor' in milestone 30th season
items.summary: The 30th season of ABC's "The Bachelor" that will premiere in March 2027 will star the former Notre Dame standout.

items.headline: Wake Forest claims 'Bachelor U' status after Sam Hartman news
items.summary: Wake Forest football is the only program, the school says, to have had three former players feature in "The Bachelor" franchise.

items.headline: Aguilar (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Rams on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: With Jacoby Brissett being traded to Baltimore on Nov. 6 and Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) out for the rest of the season, the Cardinals overhauled their QB room by signing both Josh Johnson and Aguilar earlier this week, with Carson Beck now serving as the starter. As the emergency third quarterback, Aguilar is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Beck and Johnson leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.
items.summary: With Bam Knight back in the lineup in Week 10 after one absence due to a concussion, Allgeier didn't reach double-digit touches for the first time since Week 5, a span in which the latter's 65 touches went for 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Knight himself found a similar lack of success Sunday with just 19 yards on his five rushes. Because the Cardinals racked up just 123 yards of offense in rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start, it's tough to envision worse outcomes moving forward, though the team does take on the surging Chiefs next Sunday on the road.

items.headline: Bowman reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Bowman was elevated to the active roster prior to Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks, failing to record any stats while playing four snaps with the special-teams unit. The tight end is eligible to be elevated one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and he's caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't inspire much confidence heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle.
items.summary: Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck as the starting quarterback. The offense struggled to move the ball and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck) out for the rest of the season, he should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Ford reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Ford was elevated to the active roster for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks, but he did not appear in the game. The running back could be elevated again in Week 10 versus the Rams if Bam Knight (concussion) remains sidelined.

items.headline: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Hull failed to haul in his lone target during the Cardinals' 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.summary: Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Johnson will head to Arizona in what will mark the 15th different NFL organization that he's been a part of since entering the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008. The 40-year-old is expected to operate as the primary backup option behind rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who is poised to make his first NFL start Week 10 versus the Rams in place of the injured Gardner Minshew (elbow). With Minshew at risk of missing the remainder of the 2026 campaign while he recovers from a torn UCL, Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season concludes.

items.headline: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Jones was elevated to the Cardinals' active roster for Week 10 against the Rams on Sunday. He played seven offensive snaps and failed to haul in his lone target from Carson Beck, and Jones also recorded a tackle on linebacker Wesley Bailey midway through the third quarter in what was a 34-6 loss for Arizona. Michael Wilson (neck), Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are all on season-ending IR, so Jones could be elevated to the Cardinals' active roster for Week 11 against the Chiefs on Sunday.

items.headline: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

items.headline: Long (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: Long was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the sixth-year pro has been cleared to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He will operate in a rotational role at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.

items.headline: McBride tallied five catches on as many targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: McBride's streak of at least seven catches ended at 11 games, and his receiving yardage total marked his second-fewest of the campaign in what doubled as rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start. Better days likely are ahead for the duo, but as McBride works with his third signal-caller this season -- and the least experienced one at that after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew -- there may be more lows than highs for the tight end over the final seven contests. McBride will look to bounce back next Sunday at Kansas City.

items.headline: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against Kansas City.

items.headline: Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that he has no new updates on the status of Conner (foot), who is still "working to return to perform," Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports. "It was not a good injury," LaFleur said.
items.summary: Conner hasn't played in a game since Week 3 of last season, when he sustained a right foot/ankle injury that required surgery. Though he was able to participate in individual drills in training camp, he never advanced to team work before being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return Aug. 30. The Cardinals still haven't cleared Conner to practice nearly three months later, which suggests that he either experienced a setback over the summer or plateaued in his recovery. Whatever the case, Conner doesn't seem close to a return, and the chances of him playing at any point this season will grow dimmer with each week that he doesn't practice.

items.headline: Bell was signed to the Cardinals' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Bell will head to Arizona after being cut from the Raiders' practice squad in late September. The wide receiver will provide the Cardinals with an experienced depth option moving forward.

items.headline: Dorsett signed with the Cardinals' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Dorsett has spent most of the past two seasons with Las Vegas' practice squad. He was cut Nov. 6 and has quickly found a new home with the Cardinals. Dorsett could be elevated as soon as this week, as Arizona is working with a depleted wideout corps after No. 1 option Michael Wilson (neck) joined Kendrick Bourne (tibia) on injured reserve Tuesday. However, Dorsett doesn't exactly have a recent history of success -- he hasn't logged an NFL regular-season snap since 2023 and hasn't caught a pass since 2022.

items.headline: Arizona signed Means to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Just one day after the Chiefs cut him from their practice squad, Means is already getting another shot with a new team. After recently placing Michael Wilson (neck) on IR, the Cardinals have arguably the most unproven group of wide receivers in the NFL, so if Means is elevated relatively soon, he'll have a chance to compete for targets from rookie quarterback Carson Beck right away.

items.headline: Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.summary: Branch missed a Week 9 loss to the Bengals and didn't practice this week. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair took on extra snaps in Branch's absence last week. The good news for Branch is that Atlanta has a bye coming up after Sunday's game.

items.headline: Collins (hip) is listed as active Sunday against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

items.headline: Dalton is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chiefs but was designated as his team's emergency third quarterback.
items.summary: Dalton remains the third option behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa. The "Red Rifle" will only enter Sunday's game if both Penix and Tagovailoa must exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

items.headline: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
items.summary: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

items.headline: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

items.headline: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
items.summary: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.
items.summary: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

items.headline: Robinson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

items.headline: Ali played all 19 of his snaps on special teams in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
items.summary: For the second week in a row, Ali was deployed exclusively on special teams while the Ravens leaned on Derrick Henry and Justice Hill to handle all the snaps out of the backfield. Ali has logged just seven total snaps on offense all season, carrying six times for 24 yards.

items.headline: Andrews brought in all eight targets for 82 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
items.summary: According to Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site, Andrews confirmed after Monday's game that he's been playing through a broken left hand since Week 3, but he finally appears to be back to full health. Though he didn't miss any time due to broken hand, he was listed on the injury report from Weeks 4 through 9 before avoiding the report entirely for Week 10. He proceeded to deliver a season-best performance in starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett's team debut, eclipsing his previous-best mark in receiving yardage by 33 yards. Andrews' instant chemistry with Brissett was certainly encouraging after the Ravens' passing attack's moribund state over the prior two contests, and the veteran tight end could continue thriving in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers, especially now that he appears to have fully healed up from the hand injury.

items.headline: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
items.summary: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

items.headline: Cuevas caught all three of his targets for 37 yards during Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers.
items.summary: Cuevas had an immediate connection with new starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, reeling in at least three passes for the second time this season and the first time since Week 6. The tight end ranked fourth at his position with 11 offensive snaps, sitting behind Mark Andrews (40), Matthew Hibner (22) and Nick Vannett (14). Cuevas has now caught 13 of 16 targets for 171 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.
items.summary: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

items.headline: Hill turned three carries into four yards and added five catches on seven targets for 34 yards during the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday.
items.summary: Hill also had a 14-yard carry midway through the first quarter, but the play was nullified by an offensive holding call. The veteran running back connected on a 17-yard catch with Jacoby Brissett late in the third, which set up a 36-yard field goal by Riley Patterson four plays later. Hill's five catches were a season high, and even with the Ravens' quarterback carousel over the last three weeks, the 2019 fourth-rounder has hauled in at least three passes in each of his last five outings. Losers of five straight games, the Ravens will look to turn their fortunes around in a Week 11 road tilt against the Panthers on Sunday.

items.headline: Lane brought in three of 11 targets for 61 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
items.summary: Lane was far from efficient during his first opportunity to work with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but he parlayed his career-high target total into a career-best yardage tally. The fact the rookie third-round pick garnered so much of Brissett's attention was certainly encouraging, and Lane could emerge as a much more consistent No. 3 option in the offense in coming weeks.

items.headline: Moore reverted to the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Moore was elevated to the active roster ahead of Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers and failed to reel in his only target while playing five snaps on offense. He did notch 82 yards as a kick returner, and he can be elevated one more time before the team would have to officially add him to the active roster.

items.headline: The Ravens reinstated Randall (neck/hamstring) from injured reserve Wednesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: With the rookie fifth-round pick's 21-day evaluation window coming to a close Wednesday, Baltimore added him to the 53-man roster to ensure that he'll be available to play over the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 240-pound Randall has been a full participant in practices since Week 8 and should be healthy enough to play Sunday at Carolina, but it's unclear if Baltimore will make him active for that contest. Randall will likely slot in third on the depth chart at running back behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill, and Rasheen Ali is a key contributor on special teams who could be prioritized ahead of Randall on game days.

items.headline: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback Monday night versus the Chargers.
items.summary: Slovis will operate as Baltimore's third option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Joe Fagnano are removed from the contest.

items.headline: Vannett reverted to the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Vannett was elevated to the active roster ahead of Monday night's 23-20 loss to the Chargers, and he didn't record any stats while playing 14 snaps on offense and six snaps with the special-teams unit. The tight end has appeared in each of the team's last six contests, and he seems likely to be active for Sunday's matchup with the Panthers.

items.headline: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

items.headline: Buechele reverted to the Bills' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Buechele was inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets. The journeyman could see another elevated for Sunday's Week 11 game against the Jets to serve as an emergency option behind Josh Allen and Kyle Allen.

items.headline: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
