items.headline: Bech caught two of seven targets for 10 yards during the Raiders' 21-13 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
items.summary: Bech was the favorite target of rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza, who was making his first career start Sunday after the Raiders shipped Kirk Cousins to the Vikings at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Bech's seven targets were a season high, but he mustered only two catches for his efforts, and he failed to connect on each of the last four passes he saw from Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The volume appears to be there for Bech, and he could take on a larger role offensively in Week 11 against the Broncos on Nov. 22 if star tight end Brock Bowers (ankle) is unable to play.

items.headline: Benson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: Benson is a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week. The rookie sixth-rounder has failed to find a place in a wide-open receiving corps so far, and it remains to be seen how coach Klint Kubiak will utilize him.

items.headline: Jeanty turned his nine carries into just 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 46 yards during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: After reaching the 10-carry threshold in each of the first six games of the season, Jeanty has failed to do so in four straight contests, and he also has fallen shy of 30 rushing yards in six consecutive outings. Rookie RB Mike Washington continued to split the backfield with Jeanty in Week 10, turning his nine touches into 27 yards from scrimmage. Considering recent trends, Jeanty is difficult to trust for consistent production without a boost in work.

items.headline: Laube played all 22 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and returned two kickoffs for 46 yards and one punt for zero yards.
items.summary: Since earning seven touches in a Week 5 blowout loss to the Patriots, Laube has been an afterthought on offense. He's played just eight total offense snaps in the Raiders' ensuing five games, and Sunday marked the first time all season that he was limited exclusively to special teams.

items.headline: Mayer caught two of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Jack Bech (seven targets) was the only Las Vegas player to see more than four targets in Fernando Mendoza's first career start. The rookie quarterback targeted 10 different players on his 29 attempts. With Kirk Cousins' efficiency off to Minnesota, Mayer is a low-floor TE2 for fantasy, but he could get a bit of a boost if Brock Bowers' ankle injury causes him to miss time.

items.headline: Nailor recorded one reception for minus-1 yard on four targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Making his first NFL start, No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza was under siege throughout the afternoon, as a ferocious Seahawks defense sacked him six times and limited him to just 143 passing yards on 29 attempts. As a result, Nailor and the Raiders' other pass catchers were held quiet, with running back Ashton Jeanty (four receptions for 46 yards) being the only Las Vegas player to top two catches and 25 receiving yards. Though Mendoza will get some more favorable matchups over the Raiders' final seven games, Nailor will be difficult to count on for production. Even while Kirk Cousins served as the starting quarterback for Las Vegas before being traded to the Vikings last week, Nailor was limited to just 14 receptions for 122 yards and one touchdown on 28 targets through eight appearances.

items.headline: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.

items.headline: Runyon reverted to the Raiders' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Runyon logged two offensive snaps and 18 special-teams snaps in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks. The tight end did not appear in the box score over his 20 snaps.

items.headline: Thornton (back) was a full participant in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Thornton is healthy again after sitting out the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks due to a back injury. However, it is still unlikely that the 23-year-old plays in Sunday's matchup versus the Broncos, as Thornton had been a healthy scratch every week since returning from injured reserve in late October prior to Week 10.

items.headline: Tucker caught one pass for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: In Fernando Mendoza's first career start at quarterback, Tucker saw just 6.9 percent of the targets, while Jack Bech led the team with seven looks. Tucker looks like someone who won't be usable in fantasy until he shows some tangible chemistry with the young quarterback.

items.headline: Washington compiled eight rushes for 23 yards and secured his only target for four yards during Sunday's 21-13 defeat to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Aside from a 25-carry outburst in Week 8 at the Jets, Washington has logged 54 rushes along with four catches in nine appearances, which amounts to 6.4 touches per game. Despite that number, he continues to eat into the overall backfield picture, as lead runner Ashton Jeanty failed to tally double-digit rushes for a fourth straight contest Sunday. Washington should retain a modest role alongside Jeanty next Sunday at Denver.

items.headline: Young went without a target while playing one of the Raiders' 59 snaps on offense in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. He also brought back one kickoff for 29 yards.
items.summary: Young has suited up in each of the Raiders' 10 games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams. He's seen single-digit snaps on offense in five straight games and has posted a collective 2-36-0 receiving line on three targets on the campaign.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Rypien to the practice squad Monday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: With Kirk Cousins now with the Vikings, the addition of Rypien bolsters the Raiders' depth at quarterback behind rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza and backup Aidan O'Connell. Rypien spent time earlier in the season on the Buccaneers' practice squad and had previously been with the Texans for the final two weeks of training camp before being cut in late August.

items.headline: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.

items.headline: Deguara signed with the Chargers' practice squad Thursday.
items.summary: The tight end was cut from Seattle's practice squad in late October. He did see action in one NFL regular-season game earlier in the year with Philadelphia, playing on 21 special-teams snaps.

items.headline: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
items.summary: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
items.summary: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
items.summary: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

items.headline: Kolar (concussion) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice.
items.summary: The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

items.headline: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
items.summary: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

items.headline: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.summary: McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.headline: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
items.summary: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
items.summary: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash after being listed as doubtful following a third consecutive DNP on Saturday, and it's no surprise the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

items.headline: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
items.summary: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

items.headline: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
items.summary: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

items.headline: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

items.headline: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

items.headline: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

items.headline: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

items.headline: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

items.headline: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

items.headline: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

items.headline: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

items.headline: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

items.headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Smith caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
items.summary: With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

items.headline: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

items.headline: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

items.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains optimistic Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.
items.summary: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

items.headline: Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

items.headline: The Rams signed Scott to the practice squad Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: With Jordan Whittington (back), Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined, the Rams are looking to bolster depth within the receiving corps. While Scott is on the practice squad at the moment, there's a chance he could get on the field for at least one regular-season contest. The 25-year-old appeared in a combined 28 regular-season games for the Bears in 2023 and 2024, totaling 18 catches (33 targets) for 173 yards.

items.headline: Allen turned his lone carry into zero yards and hauled in his lone target for minus-4 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Allen found the ball on both of his offensive snaps during Sunday's loss, although he ended up losing four yards on his only catch of the game early in the second quarter. He's well behind Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright on the running back depth chart, and most of Allen's playing time in Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22, likely will come on special teams.

items.headline: Bell (knee) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: After being sidelined first time this season during this past Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts, Bell told Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post that his absence was a result of hyperextending his knee in a recent practice. The rookie wideout appears to be healthier in Week 11, however, as he was able to practice in a limited fashion for a second straight day. Bell expects be available for Sunday's game against the Bills, per Furones.

items.headline: Coleman logged one catch for six yards on six targets in Sunday's Week 10 loss to Indianapolis.
items.summary: Coleman couldn't get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who made his first NFL regular-season appearance. In fact, Coleman has been quiet inefficient regardless of who has thrown him the ball this year, as he has just nine receptions on 27 targets through nine games. Two of his nine catches have been touchdowns, but he's not getting enough touches to be a trustworthy fantasy option.

items.headline: Cook was signed to the Dolphins' active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: Cook served as the team's No. 2 option at quarterback behind Kyle McCord in the team's 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, with Malik Willis (abdomen) being placed on injured reserve prior to the contest. Cook reverted to the practice squad Monday, but he has now officially become a member of the team's active roster ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

items.headline: Dulcich failed to haul in either of his two targets while logging 42 of 69 offensive snaps in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Second-year signal-caller Kyle McCord threw for 209 yards on 32 attempts in his first NFL start, but he couldn't forge much of a connection with Dulcich, who was held without a catch for the second time this season. With Malik Willis (core) out for at least three more contests while on injured reserve, Dulcich will have more time to build a rapport with McCord, but the tight end was far from a reliable fantasy option even when Willis was directing the offense. Despite playing more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in each of the Dolphins' nine games, Dulcich has been limited to 24 receptions for 270 yards and has yet to find the end zone.

items.headline: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

items.headline: Reagor reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Reagor played eight offensive snaps and was unable to haul in his sole target during Sunday's loss to the Colts. The wide receiver also logged one special-teams snap in the contest.

items.headline: Tolbert caught both of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: The wideout was active for just the fifth time in nine games this season and played 11 of 69 offensive snaps. He ran only five routes and caught a 34-yard touchdown from fellow receiver Malik Washington on a trick play early in the second quarter. Tolbert has no fantasy appeal moving forward, as he has just four catches for 79 yards on six targets this season.

items.headline: Traore went without a target while playing six of the Dolphins' 69 snaps on offense in Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
items.summary: Meanwhile, Traore tied a season-high with 23 snaps on special teams, where he continues to receive the bulk of his playing time. The reserve tight end has played in all nine of the Dolphins' games to date but has gone without a reception while being targeted once across 39 total snaps on offense.

items.headline: Washington reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Washington played five offensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Lions and caught his only target for eight yards. It was his first career regular-season NFL grab in what was Washington's 17th game.

items.headline: Wayne (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Wayne sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis with a quad injury, and his availability for Week 11 is now in question. If he's not able to get back onto the practice field Thursday or Friday, he'll be trending toward missing Sunday's game at Buffalo.

items.headline: Wright turned three carries into minus-2 yards, caught both of his targets for 17 yards and returned four kickoffs for 88 yards during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Wright's first touch on offense came midway through the second quarter and resulted in a carry for minus-3 yards, although he did connect with Kyle McCord for a 16-yard catch late in the third. Wright was on the field for 12 of the Dolphins' 69 offensive snaps (17.4 percent), which was far behind lead back Ollie Gordon (49 snaps). Wright is averaging only 1.6 YPC on 25 rushes through seven regular-season games, and most of his on-field impact has come on special teams as a returner on kickoffs. The Dolphins will stay on the road for Week 11 against the Bills on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Boyd was signed to the Dolphins' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Boyd will head to Miami after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign so far as a free agent. The wide receiver signed with the Jaguars as an undrafted free agent in April after a collegiate career with Minnesota and Texas Tech, but he was ultimately waived in late August. Boyd will now have a chance to impress with Miami and potentially earn an elevation to the active roster down the road this season.

items.headline: Bartholomew caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
items.summary: With T.J. Hockenson (wrist) inactive, Bartholomew played 53 of 69 offensive snaps against Green Bay and caught the second of Kirk Cousins' two touchdowns, scoring from 20 yards out in the fourth quarter to give Minnesota a comfortable 27-10 lead. While Ben Yurosek got the start, Bartholomew played 13 more snaps and out-targeted Yurosek four to one. Cousins has an affinity for throwing to his tight ends, so Bartholomew will be on the fantasy radar if Hockenson needs to miss more time.

items.headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Brosmer was the Vikings' backup for Week 9 against the Bills and ended up seeing the field late in the fourth quarter, when he completed six of seven pass attempts for 58 yards. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and he will serve as Minnesota's starter Sunday while Carson Wentz operates as the backup. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) sidelined, that leaves Brosmer as the emergency QB3, which prohibits the latter from playing unless both Cousins and Wentz leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Culp reverted to the Vikings' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Culp will return to the practice squad after he was elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end didn't record any stats while playing 13 snaps on special teams, and he could be elevated again in Week 11 if T.J. Hockenson (wrist) remains sidelined against the 49ers.

items.headline: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

items.headline: Felton is on track to operate in a more prominent role in Week 11 versus the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Felton drew a start in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, reeling in a season-high three of five targets for 33 yards over 56 offensive snaps. The wide receiver stepped into a starting role as a result of Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) being sidelined, and Addison is now reportedly set to undergo surgery to address his injury, opening the door for more opportunities for Felton moving forward.

items.headline: Hockenson (wrist) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
items.summary: After sitting out this past Sunday's win at Green Bay due to wrist and chest injuries, Hockenson has logged back-to-back capped sessions to begin Week 11 prep due to just the wrist issue. He'll have one more opportunity to get back to full Friday, at which point the Vikings may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Jones (shoulder) off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
items.summary: Jones was elevated from the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster for both Week 5 and Week 10 against the Saints and Packers, respectively, and he'll now be part of Minnesota's 53-man roster moving forward. He picked up a shoulder injury during Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay and was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, so his reps over the coming days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the 49ers on Nov. 22. The addition of Jones to the active roster gives the Vikings extra depth at wide receiver in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb).

items.headline: Mason carried the ball 16 times for 59 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
items.summary: The fifth-year RB led the Vikings in rushing yards, but Aaron Jones was the more productive player in the backfield, gaining 55 scrimmage yards on 12 touches and scoring on a one-yard plunge in the second quarter. Mason has yet to get into the end zone in four games since returning from a thumb injury, piecing together 182 rushing yards on 4.0 yards per carry while working in a timeshare with Jones. He could break that drought in Week 11 in a potential revenge game against the 49ers.

items.headline: Murray (hamstring) will miss Wednesday's practice, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
items.summary: The Vikings are targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Falcons on Sunday, Nov. 29, for Murray to be available again, so his lack of activity this week doesn't come as a susprise. Whenever Murray is back, though, he likely will take on No. 2 QB duties due to the arrival of Kirk Cousins from Las Vegas at the trade deadline.

items.headline: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Claiborne (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Bankston to the practice squad Wednesday, Rob Kleifield of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Bankston was cut from the Packers' practice squad Oct. 20, but the New Mexico product will find a new home with the Vikings and stay in the NFC North division. He was with Minnesota during the tail end of the 2025 season and was with the Giants in training camp before being cut by New York on Aug. 29. Bankston's addition gives the Vikings additional backfield depth and a potential contributor on special teams.

items.headline: Beckham signed with the Vikings' practice squad Thursday
items.summary: Beckham rejoins the Vikings after being released by the team earlier in the week. The veteran was active for Monday Night Football in Week 9 but played only two snaps. He'll remain in the system and could be called up to the active roster if and when the Vikings need more depth at receiver.

items.headline: Minnesota signed Eskridge to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Eskridge has been a free agent since the offseason, but he's now getting a fresh opportunity with a new club. Over 13 games with the Dolphins in 2025, he caught four of seven targets for 62 yards while also contributing as a kick returner. With Jordan Addison set to miss some time after undergoing surgery on his thumb, it makes sense that the Vikings would add some organizational depth at wide receiver.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Lauter to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding moves, the Saints also signed tight end Treyton Welch to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Lauter started with the Raiders as an undrafted free agent during the offseason and is still waiting to make his regular-season NFL debut.

items.headline: Brown (hamstring) was spotted walking around with a limp in the locker room following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
items.summary: Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

items.headline: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
items.summary: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

items.headline: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
items.summary: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
items.summary: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

items.headline: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

items.headline: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
items.summary: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

items.headline: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
items.summary: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but available as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: As he has for the first nine games of his career, Morton only will see the field if both starter Drake Maye and backup Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
items.summary: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

items.headline: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
items.summary: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Arkin to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The tight end was cut from the 53-man roster Monday and cleared waivers. The undrafted rookie has appeared in five games for New England this season but hasn't been targeted on 60 offensive snaps. Arkin has played another 41 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
items.summary: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

items.headline: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

items.headline: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

items.headline: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
items.summary: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

items.headline: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
items.summary: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

items.headline: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

items.headline: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

items.headline: White reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With Travis Etienne (IR, hamstring) still sidelined and Kendre Miller cut over the weekend, White was elevated as the RB3 behind Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime. White played four offensive snaps against Cleveland on Sunday and rushed one time for five yards.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
items.summary: Wilson is the No. 3 quarterback behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. The inactive third option will only enter Sunday's game if Shough and Rattler must leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Welch to its practice squad Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: In corresponding transactions, the Saints also signed tight end Matt Lauter to their practice squad and released tight end Stone Smartt (undisclosed) from their practice squad with an injury designation. Welch has already suited up for five games with New Orleans this season, with most of his snaps coming on special teams.

items.headline: Desrosiers carried the ball three times for 20 yards during the Giants' win over the Eagles on Sunday.
items.summary: Desrosiers made his regular-season debut during the victory, serving as the team's No. 2 running back behind Devin Singletary, as Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury. With Skattebo now healthy again, Desrosiers will likely be relegated to a depth role during Thursday's matchup versus the Commanders.

items.headline: Fidone (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's contest in Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Fidone suited up for each of New York's previous three games before a Week 8 bye, but he's a healthy scratch against the Eagles. The second-year tight end has worked mostly on special teams this season and has one catch for 29 yards on one target over three contests. Fidone figures to be at risk for inactive status when the three tight ends ahead of him in the pecking order -- Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz -- are healthy.

items.headline: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
items.summary: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
items.summary: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.

items.headline: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

items.headline: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
items.summary: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Mafah reverted to the Giants' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With both Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Tyrone Tracy (IR, hamstring) sidelined, Mafah joined Greg Desrosiers as the healthy running backs behind Devin Singletary. Mafah played just 10 snaps on special teams and none on offense Sunday against Philly.

items.headline: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
items.summary: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

items.headline: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
items.summary: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

items.headline: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

items.headline: The Giants released Gray from their practice squad Tuesday, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Gray had signed to New York's practice squad Nov. 2, but he apparently didn't impress enough to remain in the organization for long. The 2023 fifth-round draft pick has yet to see regular-season action this year after spending his first four campaigns with the Giants. Gray will likely have to settle for another practice-squad deal in order to get an opportunity with another organization.

items.headline: The Giants signed Haener to their practice squad Saturday,Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Haener has been part of New York's active roster twice this season, and he was most recently waived by the team Thursday. The Fresno State product will remain in the organization on the practice squad, as the Giants have J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston as their quarterbacks on game days. Should one of those two get injured and need to miss time, Haener figures to be elevated or signed to the roster again.

items.headline: The Giants signed Jones to their practice squad Wednesday, Dan Salomone and Matt Citak of the team's official site report.
items.summary: Jones was waived from the Giants' active roster Monday, but after going unclaimed, he's decided to stay with the organization as a member of the practice squad. Over six games with the G-Men so far this year, he's caught two of three targets for 66 yards while also returning some kicks and punts.

items.headline: Allen rushed eight times for 40 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: For a second consecutive game, Allen was outplayed by Breece Hall, who produced 108 scrimmage yards on 15 touches. Allen remains the more efficient runner, averaging 5.0 yards per carry to Hall's 3.4 this season, but Hall is the team's preferred option in passing situations, which have been plentiful with the 2-8 Jets frequently in catch-up mode. Perhaps a Week 11 matchup with a Chargers team that's still searching for its first win through Sunday of Week 10 will offer an opportunity to stick with the run and play to Allen's strengths.

items.headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Cooper (ankle/hip) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
items.summary: Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

items.headline: Davis didn't touch the ball on offense in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: With Breece Hall and Braelon Allen both healthy, Davis has minimal fantasy value, except for leagues that count return yardage. He's played zero offensive snaps over the last two contests, but Davis did return three kickoffs for 74 yards against Buffalo.

items.headline: Hall rushed 11 times for 41 yards and caught all four of his targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: Hall narrowly topped Braelon Allen (eight carries for 40 yards) for the team lead in rushing yards and finished second behind Garrett Wilson (seven catches for 106 yards) in both receptions and receiving yards. While Allen continues to be more efficient as a rusher, Hall's superior receiving ability should help the latter maintain the edge in playing time for a 2-8 Jets team that often finds itself playing catch-up. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik, who played most of the second half Sunday, could be more reliant on check downs to Hall than veteran Geno Smith (ankle) was, but it remains to be seen who will get the nod under center in Week 11 against the Chargers.

items.headline: Mitchell caught three passes for 59 yards on eight targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: With Garrett Wilson back from his one-game absence Sunday, Mitchell was left fighting for secondary looks. His eight targets were second on the team, trailing Wilson's 14, and Omar Cooper's early-game ankle injury helped Mitchell's volume solidify. If Cooper is going to miss time going forward, Mitchell will be a more comfortable fantasy WR3 play with upside headed into next Sunday's game against the Chargers.

items.headline: Sadiq was limited to a three-yard reception on two targets in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills.
items.summary: On a day in which quarterbacks Geno Smith (ankle) and Cade Klubnik dropped back 45 times, Sadiq wasn't able to see much involvement in the passing game. Though the rookie first-round pick put his pass-catching chops on display with a 7-105-1 receiving line in Week 3 against Detroit, he's since delivered a collective 10-95-0 line on 19 targets over the Jets' ensuing seven contests. A lack of extended playing time has been a factor in Sadiq's listless production of late; he's logged fewer than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in five of those seven games while second-year tight end Mason Taylor typically has handled larger snap shares.

items.headline: Taylor caught all four of his targets for 20 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
items.summary: Taylor's four catches were tied with Breece Hall and Isaiah Williams for second most on the Jets behind Garrett Wilson, who turned 14 targets into a 7-106-1 line. It was the third time this season that Taylor recorded at least four catches, with his last instance being Week 7 against the Dolphins (five receptions). The second-year tight end has a 22-167-2 line on 29 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.
items.summary: With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

items.headline: Patrick (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bills.
items.summary: Garrett Wilson (concussion), Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) have all been cleared to play Sunday, so Patrick will observe from the sidelines. Patrick hasn't played since Week 7 against the Dolphins, and his next opportunity to suit up is Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday.
items.summary: It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.

items.headline: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

items.headline: Covey (knee) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game versus the Giants.
items.summary: Covey was again unable to practice during the week because of the knee injury he suffered back in Week 7 versus the Cowboys, and he'll miss his second straight game in Week 9. In his absence, 2025 fifth-rounder Jaydon Blue and 2024 second-rounder Cooper DeJean will likely continue to see increased opportunities in the return game.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
items.summary: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

items.headline: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

items.headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

items.headline: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
items.summary: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

items.headline: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

items.headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: The Eagles released Pierce (undisclosed) from IR with an injury settlement Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.summary: Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another organization.

items.headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday.
items.summary: Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.

items.headline: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
items.summary: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

items.headline: Wicks (ankle) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
items.summary: Wicks is seeking his first game action since Week 6 due to an ankle injury, and he still has some work to do after kicking off Week 11 prep with back-to-back capped sessions. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to play Sunday versus the Steelers.

items.headline: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.
items.summary: Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Rucci to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Rucci last spent time with the Chargers before being let go by the team ahead of Week 10. In six games with the Bolts, the 27-year-old recorded one reception for seven yards and a touchdown. The second-year pro will act as organizational depth after Zach Ertz was elevated to the active roster.

items.headline: The Eagles signed Skinner to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Skinner was cut by the Eagles in early November after landing on the team's practice squad one week prior. Depending on the statuses of Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Skinner may be elevated for extra depth at wide receiver in Week 11.

items.headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

items.headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
items.summary: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

items.headline: Freiermuth recorded two catches (on three targets) for 35 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 38-18 loss in Cincinnati.
items.summary: Freiermuth was added to the Steelers' injury report Saturday due to an illness that left him questionable for Week 10 action. Ultimately, he avoided inactive status and also made an end-zone visit for the first time since Week 5 on a 27-yard hookup with QB Aaron Rodgers in the fourth quarter. Considering Freiermuth hasn't reached 50 receiving yards in any game this season, he remains a TD-dependent fantasy option (five in his nine appearances).

items.headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.
items.summary: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.
items.summary: Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.

items.headline: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
