items.summary: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

items.headline: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
items.summary: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

items.headline: Washington caught one pass for five yards on two targets in Sunday night's loss to the Bengals.
items.summary: Aaron Rodgers threw for 143 yards in the game, and most of that came in garbage time in the second half with the score already out of hand. Washington has fewer than 30 receiving yards in seven of nine games played this season and is the epitome of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at tight end.

items.headline: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
items.summary: After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

items.headline: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.summary: With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

items.headline: The Steelers activated Hurleman (undisclosed) from the practice squad injured list Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hurleman landed on the practice squad IL in mid-September due to an undisclosed injury. The Notre Dame product is now fully healthy, and he would be a candidate for elevation to the Steelers' active roster if the team needs more depth at running back. Hurleman has yet to play in a regular-season game since entering the NFL in May of 2025 as an undrafted free agent.

items.headline: Cooks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
items.summary: Mike Evans (Achilles) is also inactive for a third consecutive game, but Cooks' services are not needed Sunday due to the return of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the acquisition of Keenan Allen from the Colts on Tuesday. It's unclear if Cooks will have any role in the 49ers' offense once Evans is cleared to return. For now, Cooks' next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Cowing did not draw any targets during Sunday's 46-40 win at Dallas.
items.summary: Cowing was also sent back to receive two punts in Week 10, making a fair catch on one and allowing the other to go into the endzone for a touchback. He has now drawn just one target over the two games following his three-catch performance in Week 7, and his role in the 49ers' offense figures to shrink even further once veteran Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis, which could happen as soon as Sunday versus Minnesota.

items.headline: Hodge reverted to the 49ers' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: With the Niners still dealing with several injuries at wide receiver, Hodge appeared in his fourth game this season and played 12 offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Raiders. He caught his lone target for 17 yards and has two grabs for 35 yards this season.

items.headline: James returned five kickoffs for 101 yards during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: James set the tone right out of halftime with a 49-yard kickoff return, although the yards gained were mitigated by a holding penalty by the Niners. All eight of his snaps came on special teams, and it looks like the second-year pro is out of the mix for backfield touches behind RB1 Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, the latter of whom found the end zone for the second time in his last three outings. The 49ers will travel to Mexico City for Week 11 to face the Vikings on Nov. 22.

items.headline: Jones (illness) did not participate at practice Thursday.
items.summary: Jones popped up on the 49ers' injury report with an unspecified illness Wednesday, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. If he can't practice in full Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

items.headline: Kittle brought in six of nine targets for 74 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: Kittle put together a very solid fantasy performance that was easily lost in the shuffle of multiple spectacular efforts by players on either side. However, the veteran tight end did pace the 49ers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and he's now recorded at least 70 yards on five occasions this season. Kittle is up to a 44-557-5 line on 62 targets through nine games as a Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday night approaches.

items.headline: Robinson played 21 of 65 offensive snaps (32.3 percent) but didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: Robinson's snap count was fourth-most among San Francisco's wide receivers, but his role in the offense shrunk due to the return of Deebo Samuel and the acquisition of Keenan Allen at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Brandin Cooks (coach's decision) was a healthy scratch for Week 10, and Robinson could join the former on the sidelines for Week 11 against the Vikings on Nov. 22, if veteran wide receiver Mike Evans (Achilles) is cleared to return for that contest.

items.headline: Guerendo (pectoral) was working off to the side during practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.

items.headline: Kirk announced Wednesday via his personal Instagram account that he recently underwent meniscus surgery.
items.summary: After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

items.headline: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

items.headline: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

items.headline: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
items.summary: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

items.headline: Foster reverted to the Seahawks' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Foster logged his first career regular-season offensive snaps in Sunday's win over the Cardinals but didn't touch the ball on five plays he was in for. He's appeared in three contests for Seattle this season, seeing 10 snaps on special teams.

items.headline: Holani is week-to-week after suffering an MCL sprain in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday.
items.summary: Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

items.headline: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

items.headline: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
items.summary: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.
items.summary: Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

items.headline: The Seahawks released Jones on Friday, Howard Balzer of USA Today reports. He was then signed back to the team's practice squad, per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com.
items.summary: Jones has been dealing with a hamstring injury and was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday after missing Monday's loss to the Bears. He didn't appear on the practice report Friday because Seattle decided to let the veteran running back go. However, Jones agreed to re-sign as part of the club's practice squad later in the day, so he'll now serve as depth in case injuries strike the Seahawks' running-back room again.

items.headline: Daniels is slated to take all of the first-teams reps Wednesday with Baker Mayfield (foot) sidelined for the Buccaneers' first Week 11 practice, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.summary: While the Buccaneers aren't ruling Mayfield out from playing Sunday in Detroit, the fact that he'll be a spectator in practice coming out of a Week 10 bye suggests that Daniels has the early edge on the Week 11 start. Per Auman, Mayfield appeared to be walking normally off to the side during Wednesday's practice, which could indicate that he'll attempt to test out his strained foot during Thursday's session. The Buccaneers should have some clarity by Friday whether Daniels or Mayfield will draw the start Sunday, with Mayfield's activity (or lack thereof) over the next two days likely to be the determining factor.

items.headline: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

items.headline: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
items.summary: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

items.headline: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

items.headline: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

items.headline: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
items.summary: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

items.headline: The Buccaneers signed Stick off their practice squad Monday, Scott Smith of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Stick has been a member of the Buccaneers' practice squad all season, with Tampa Bay having previously elevated him from Weeks 4 through 6 to back up Jalon Daniels while he filled in as the starter in place of Baker Mayfield, who was out due to a dislocated thumb. Mayfield has since moved past that injury, but he's currently nursing a sprained foot coming out of the Buccaneers' Week 9 loss to the Bears. Tampa Bay's decision to sign Stick implies some concern about Mayfield's status heading into Sunday's game against the Lions, potentially setting the stage for Stick to back up Daniels for the fourth time this season.

items.headline: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
items.summary: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

items.headline: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
items.summary: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

items.headline: Rush is in line to sign with the Buccaneers' practice squad, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.summary: Rush will give Tampa Bay added QB depth with starter Baker Mayfield dealing with an injury to his foot and ankle area that he sustained in Week 9. Jalon Daniels currently is Mayfield's top backup ahead of Week 11 action, while Easton Stick is on the team's practice squad.

items.headline: Bellinger caught two of three targets for six yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: The blocking specialist played 28 of 57 offensive snaps and was asked to block on 12 of those plays. His two-yard touchdown in the second quarter was Bellinger's first of the season. For the year, Bellinger has 11 grabs for 76 yards and the score on 18 targets across nine contests.

items.headline: Chestnut played all 25 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Jaguars.
items.summary: The fifth-year running back has suited up for all nine of the Titans' games this season, but he's been deployed almost exclusively on special teams as a member of the team's kick coverage and return units. He's played just two offensive snaps on the campaign and hasn't logged any carries or targets.

items.headline: Dike caught two passes for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
items.summary: With Carnell Tate (shoulder) out again, Dike played 54 of 57 offensive snaps against Jacksonville, but his three targets were a distant fifth on the team and represented just an 8.1 percent target share. Outside of his 5-71-1 receiving outburst in Week 8 against Cincinnati, Dike has amassed eight catches for 69 scoreless yards. He's not a reliable fantasy option, though a Week 11 date with Dallas' secondary awaits should Tate remain sidelined.

items.headline: Helm caught all four of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 40-23 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: After a career day last time out in Week 8 against the Bengals, Helm's box score looked more familiar against Jacksonville's stout defense. He's been held below 30 yards in eight of nine games this season and has yet to catch a touchdown. Helm is a member of the large bucket of low-floor TE2 options in fantasy.

items.headline: Restrepo, whom the Titans signed off their practice squad Tuesday, could be in store for more playing time out of the slot moving forward after Tennessee placed Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) on injured reserve, Mark Mihalko of USA Today reports.
items.summary: A 2025 undrafted free agent who played alongside Cam Ward during their final collegiate seasons at Miami, Restrepo showed immediate chemistry with the Titans' second-year quarterback during a 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10. Restrepo went on to play 19 snaps following Robinson's exit late in the third quarter and notched three receptions for 31 yards on three targets over the game's final 10 minutes. While the Titans are expected to get rookie first-round pick Carnell Tate (shoulder) back for Sunday's game in Dallas, Restrepo's strong showing in relief of the injured Robinson last week should at least allow him to stick ahead of Calvin Ridley (four snaps in Week 10) as Tennessee's No. 4 wideout.

items.headline: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
items.summary: Singleton remains a healthy scratch for Week 10. The fifth-round rookie has played in four contests, logging seven rush attempts for 12 yards. Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears are set to continue as the main rushers for the Titans' offense.

items.headline: Spears (knee) was limited in practice Thursday.
items.summary: The running back returned to action last Sunday against the Jaguars and logged 16 snaps behind Tony Pollard's 41. Spears is only playable in Week 11 against Dallas as a desperation fantasy option.

items.headline: The Titans signed Brownlee to the practice squad Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Brownlee spent about a week on the Giants' practice squad before being cut by the team Oct. 27. He last saw regular-season action in 2025 with the Chiefs, when he saw just one target without recording a catch across six games. Titans wide receivers Carnell Tate (shoulder) and Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) are both working through injuries, although the former is expected to return from a two-game absence to play in Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday.

items.headline: The Titans waived Carter on Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Carter suited up for each of the Titans' three games prior to the Week 8 bye, but his only offensive stats came in Week 7 against the Browns, when he turned three carries into seven yards and caught his lone target for seven yards. His removal from the 53-man roster indicates that the Titans are confident that Tyjae Spears (knee) will be available for Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Jaguars. Assuming he clears waivers, Carter will have the opportunity to explore his next options and link up with a team in need of backfield depth.

items.headline: Thrash was signed to the Titans' practice squad Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Thrash was cut from the Raiders' practice squad Oct. 27, and he will now head to Tennessee. The wide receiver has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season, but he combined to catch 13 of 22 targets for 129 yards over 18 regular-season games with the Browns between 2024 and 2025. Thrash will now provide the Titans with an additional depth option at wideout after Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.

items.headline: Bradley reverted to the Commanders' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Bradley appeared in his first career regular-season game in Sunday's loss to the Rams, recording one catch for 12 yards across 17 offensive snaps. He could get some more run in the coming weeks if Dyami Brown (calf) remains sidelined for Washington.

items.headline: Burks caught two of three targets for 27 yards Thursday in a 24-21 win over the Giants.
items.summary: Burks missed Week 9 due to a foot injury but was able to limit his absence to one game. The veteran wideout logged a 60 percent offensive snap share, third among Washington wideouts behind Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams. Burks has a chance to take on a larger role in the Commanders' passing game with Terry McLaurin (knee) lost for the season, though Diggs and Williams may be better bets for weekly production given their higher spots in the pecking order.

items.headline: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

items.headline: Heath signed with the Commanders' practice squad Thursday.
items.summary: The 26-year-old wideout appeared in 37 regular-season games with the Packers from 2023 to 2025, and Heath caught 31 passes for 308 yards and three touchdowns on 44 targets during that span. He gives the Commanders some added depth at the position.

items.headline: Jefferson caught five of seven targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: With Terry McLaurin (knee) and Treylon Burks (foot) out for the Commanders, Jefferson played 36 of 62 offensive snaps and ran 25 routes on Jayden Daniels' 42 dropbacks. The veteran wideout was signed to the active roster from the practice squad two weeks ago and led the team in receiving against Los Angeles. If Burks needs to miss more time, Jefferson could again have a role in three-wide sets Thursday night against the Giants.

items.headline: Kaliakmanis (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Giants but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
items.summary: Kaliakmanis is inactive once again. However, if Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection, Kaliakmanis will be available to play.

items.headline: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
items.summary: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

items.headline: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
items.summary: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.

items.headline: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
items.summary: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

items.headline: White rushed 11 times for 47 yards and brought in one of two targets for five yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: White led the Commanders' ground attack once again, posting a team high in rushing yards and tying for the team lead in rush attempts with Jayden Daniels. The veteran back wasn't as involved as usual as a receiver, however, capping the overall quality of his fantasy performance. White also could see Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) make his return for a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23, a development that would likely relegate the former to a complementary role he'd presumably share with Austin Ekeler.

items.headline: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
items.summary: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

items.headline: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
items.summary: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

items.headline: The Commanders placed Brown (calf) on injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Brown will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a calf injury during Thursday's practice. With Treylon Burks (foot) also ruled out, Van Jefferson and Luke McCaffrey could see increased usage on offense during Sunday's matchup versus the Rams.

items.headline: Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.summary: The Commanders designated Croskey-Merritt for return from injured reserve Tuesday, and in the team's first official practice of Week 11 prep, he was uninhibited. Assuming he's able to maintain that activity level Friday and Saturday, he's a good bet to miss the minimum four games on IR due to the groin injury that bothered him multiple weeks through the first five contests of the campaign.
